title: Implement XVERIFY command: verify article CID and signature
description:
Why: archival tools and auditors want to confirm that an article stored on this server is bit-for-bit identical to a known-good CID without fetching the full body. XVERIFY checks the stored CID matches the claimed one, and optionally re-verifies the operator signature. This lets a remote tool do a lightweight integrity probe: 'do you have this CID and is it intact?'

What: XVERIFY <message-id> <expected-cid> — server looks up the stored CID for message-id, compares it to expected-cid, re-derives the CID from the stored block to confirm local integrity, and returns 291 (match) or 541 (mismatch/not found). Optionally: XVERIFY <message-id> <expected-cid> SIG also re-verifies the operator signature over the canonical bytes.
design: Response codes: 291 = verified OK, 541 = not found or CID mismatch, 542 = signature verification failed. CID re-derivation: fetch block bytes from IPFS store, compute SHA2-256 multihash, wrap as DAG-CBOR CIDv1 — must match stored CID. Signature verification: deserialize canonical bytes from block, call core::signing::verify() with operator public key. Operator public key loaded from config at startup, stored in ServerStores.
